precepts.text: Against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast, that ye may know the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel. Not even a dog may speak against you. You are the jewellery God wears around his neck, the apple of his eye; carry yourself like that even in captivity, because it is temporary. They say you do not talk like a slave because I am not one. Christ on the cross knew he could call down legions, and we are joint heirs; the world is terrified of us making that connection.
precepts.point: I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations. Whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be, and he put talents in us. That is why the Bishop stresses organizing those talents; you cannot bring self-doubt around him. Get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

precepts.text: The Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.
precepts.point: She knew the child was a Hebrew and no Egyptian because the Most High put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; though both peoples were dark of skin, this was a child of the chosen nation.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
When the daughter of Pharaoh opened the ark and saw the child, she said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.” She knew the child was a Hebrew and no Egyptian. The Lord told Pharaoh why that could be: “that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Both peoples were dark of skin, but the Most High put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel, and Pharaoh’s daughter saw it in this child.

precepts.text: The daughters of Reuel said an Egyptian delivered us; Moses was taken for an Egyptian.
precepts.point: The difference was made plain in the plague itself: the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

precepts.why:
“that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” A difference had to be shown, because Israel and the Egyptians looked alike. Nobody could tell them apart by looking.

Moses is the proof. When he delivered the daughters of Reuel at the well, they went home and said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds, and also drew water enough for us, and watered the flock.” Moses, an Israelite, was taken for an Egyptian. Joseph was mistaken for an Egyptian by his own brothers the same way.

So the Lord put the difference in the plague itself: not a dog moved his tongue against Israel, and the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people. The difference was never in the look; it was in whom the Lord spared.

precepts.text: The chief captain took Paul for that Egyptian; Israel resembled the Egyptians in appearance.
precepts.point: The difference was made plain in the plague itself: the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

precepts.why:
Long after Egypt, the resemblance was still there. When Paul was taken in Jerusalem, the chief captain asked him, “Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?” Paul, an Israelite, was taken for that Egyptian. Israel resembled the Egyptians in appearance.

That is why the Lord had to put a difference between them in Egypt. If Moses could be taken for an Egyptian, and Paul could be taken for an Egyptian, then the difference the Lord made was not one anyone could see in a face. It was shown by his hand, when not a dog moved his tongue against Israel and the firstborn of Egypt died.

precepts.text: The Canaanites saw the mourning and called it a grievous mourning to the Egyptians; Jacob's family blended in with the Egyptians among them.
precepts.point: The difference was made plain in the plague itself: the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people.

note.label: Exodus 11: The Death of the Firstborn Announced

precepts.why:
At Jacob's funeral the Canaanites saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, and “they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abel–mizraim”. The mourners were the family of Jacob, but the Canaanites called them Egyptians, because no one could tell the difference. Jacob's family blended in with the Egyptians among them.

Moses, Paul, Joseph with his own brothers, and Jacob's family at his funeral: over and over Israel was taken for Egyptians. That is why the Lord said “that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.” The difference was made plain in the plague: the houses whose firstborn died were shown not to be his people, and the houses where not a dog moved his tongue were Israel.

precepts.text: The Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel; his laws sanctify his people.
precepts.point: The Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel and sanctified his people with these laws; these laws make us special, going back to Deuteronomy 7 and 6, how he separated us. Do not follow the customs and fashions of the heathen.

note.label: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering Without Blemish

precepts.why:
In Egypt the Lord said that “against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

The Lord put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel, and He sanctified His people with these laws. The statute not to eat blood, the Egyptian custom, is part of that difference: these laws make us special.

precepts.text: Against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, that ye may know how that the LORD doth put a difference between Egypt and Israel; underline it and put Joshua 10:20-21 next to it.
precepts.point: Christ did not come for all nations; he came for one people. If in your Christian mind you decide to run to Paul to try to contradict Christ, that lets you know you are wicked, because Christ trumps everybody; and Paul did not teach opposite of Christ anyway, he taught the same thing and just used different names, Gentiles, heathen, the uncircumcised.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
“none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel.” Underline it and put Joshua 10:20-21 next to it: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Not a dog shall move his tongue against any of the children of Israel, that ye may know the Lord puts a difference between Egypt and Israel. In Joshua, after the very great slaughter, none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Those dogs equal nations. The Lord puts a difference between Israel and the nations, in Egypt and in the land of Canaan alike.
